name: ABeta Amyloidosis, Dutch Type
aliases: Hereditary Cerebral Hemorrhage with Amyloidosis-Dutch Type

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Diagnostic Criteria for Hereditary Cerebral Hemorrhage with Amyloidosis-Dutch Type

criteria.description: Identification of pathogenic mutation in the APP gene (E693Q mutation)
Recurrent lobar intracerebral hemorrhages typically beginning in mid-adulthood
Amyloid beta peptide deposition in cerebral vessel walls confirmed by biopsy or autopsy
Positive family history of similar cerebral hemorrhagic events

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of pathogenic APP gene mutation plus clinical presentation of recurrent lobar hemorrhages
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Histopathological confirmation is supportive but not mandatory if genetic and clinical criteria are met.

laboratory: CSF analysis typically normal or nonspecific
imaging: MRI showing multiple lobar cerebral hemorrhages
Gradient echo or susceptibility weighted imaging (SWI) revealing cerebral microbleeds
other: Histopathological confirmation of amyloid beta deposits in cerebral vessels

distinguishingFeatures: Typically occurs in elderly without family history
Less frequent recurrent hemorrhages at younger age
Clinical presentation similar but genetic testing differentiates

redFlags: Recurrent lobar intracerebral hemorrhages in mid-adulthood
Family history of early-onset cerebral hemorrhages
Rapidly progressive cognitive decline following hemorrhagic events
references: Levy E, et al. Hereditary cerebral hemorrhage with amyloidosis-Dutch type. Brain Pathol. 1990.
Van Broeckhoven C, et al. Mutation in the amyloid precursor protein gene associated with hereditary cerebral hemorrhage. Nature. 1990.
